plain.text: After saying goodbye, Paul and his companions sailed to Tyre. There they found disciples, who through the Spirit urged Paul not to go on to Jerusalem. When it was time to leave, everyone, with their wives and children, walked with them out of the city and knelt on the beach to pray. Then they sailed on.

At Caesarea they stayed with Philip the evangelist, who had four unmarried daughters who prophesied. A prophet named Agabus came. He took Paul's belt, tied his own hands and feet with it and said, "The Holy Spirit says, 'In this way the owner of this belt will be bound in Jerusalem and handed over to the Gentiles.'" Everyone pleaded with Paul not to go. Paul answered, "Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus." They gave up and said, "The Lord's will be done."

In Jerusalem, the believers welcomed them warmly. Paul reported to James and the elders what God had done among the Gentiles, and they praised God. They told Paul that thousands of Jewish believers, zealous for the law, had heard that he taught Jews to abandon Moses. They suggested he join four men in a purification rite and pay their expenses, to show he still lived in obedience to the law. Paul did so.

Near the end of the seven days, some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple and stirred up the crowd. They shouted that he taught against the people, the law and the temple, and claimed he had brought Greeks into the temple. The whole city was aroused. They dragged Paul out and tried to kill him. The Roman commander rushed in with soldiers. He arrested Paul, bound him with two chains and asked who he was. The crowd was so violent that the soldiers had to carry Paul up the steps, while the people shouted, "Get rid of him!"

As they were about to take him into the barracks, Paul asked the commander in Greek for permission to speak. The commander was surprised; he had thought Paul was an Egyptian rebel. Paul said, "I am a Jew, from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Please let me speak to the people." Standing on the steps, Paul motioned to the crowd, and when they were silent, he spoke to them in Aramaic.

summary.bigIdea: Knowing danger awaits, Paul goes to Jerusalem anyway, ready to suffer for Jesus, and is arrested in the temple.
points: Believers warn Paul not to go to Jerusalem; he is ready even to die.
Paul joins a purification rite to show he respects the law.
A riot breaks out in the temple, and Roman soldiers arrest Paul.
summary.reflection: Paul's friends finally said, "The Lord's will be done." When is that hard for you to say?
